slides.heading: Subarray Sort
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Subarray Sort, a hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Smallest [start, end] range which, if sorted, makes the whole array sorted; [-1, -1] if sorted.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Smallest start, end range which, if sorted, makes the whole array sorted; -1, -1 if sorted.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Find the smallest and largest values that are out of order; their correct positions bound the subarray.
slides.narration: Find the smallest and largest values that are out of order; their correct positions bound the subarray.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Sort a copy and compare → O(n log n)
Find min/max out of place, then their positions → O(n)
slides.narration: Sorting a copy and finding the first and last differences is n log n. Finding the smallest and largest out-of-order values, then where they belong, is linear.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Scan for elements out of order with a neighbour
2. Track the min and max among them
3. Find where min belongs from the left and max from the right
slides.narration: Step by step. First, scan for elements out of order with a neighbour. Second, track the min and max among them. Third, find where min belongs from the left and max from the right.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Find out-of-order elements
slides.narration: Mark every element that's smaller than its left neighbour or bigger than its right.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Smallest = 6, largest = 12
slides.narration: Among them the smallest is 6 and the largest is 12.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Answer: [3, 9]
slides.narration: 6 belongs right after the first value bigger than it, index 3. 12 belongs at index 9. Sorting indices 3 to 9 sorts the array.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We track the min and max of out-of-order elements, return minus ones if none, then move l right while values are at most min and r left while values are at least max.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Out-of-order values may be far from the boundary
slides.narration: If nothing is out of order, return minus one, minus one. Use less-or-equal so duplicates are handled.

bullets: Explain why min/max determine the bounds

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Find the smallest and largest values that are out of order; their correct positions bound the subarray.
